title: Find the Oatmeal
can_do: 在商店设定中询问商品位置，并用包装特征确认选择。

conversation_move.label: ask where to find an item in a shop

trigger: Mom needs oatmeal, but it is not on the shelf they are currently checking.
core_response: Where can we find the oatmeal?
stretch_response: Can we look for the blue box in the next aisle?
repair_response: Not that blue box. The one with the oat picture.
essential_props: two grocery boxes and a simple aisle sign

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: We need oatmeal, but I do not see it here.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Where can we find the oatmeal?

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: The sign says cereal is in the next aisle.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Can we look for the blue box there?

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: Here are two blue boxes. Which one?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: The one with the big oat picture, please.

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: That is oatmeal. We will put it in the basket.

replay_cards.title: Find the soap
replay_cards.setting: A pretend shop shelf at home
replay_cards.change: Soap is not with the snacks
replay_cards.challenge: Ask where it is, follow a simple sign clue, identify the pump bottle, and place it in the basket

replay_cards.title: Find the apples
replay_cards.setting: A real or pretend produce area
replay_cards.challenge: Ask for the produce area, describe apples rather than tomatoes, choose one, and continue shopping

parent_support: A printed word is only an adult clue; the child succeeds through asking and visual matching.
Keep the shop as a setting, not a prop-heavy reconstruction.
